findings.reason: §1 and §2 collapse from "build it" to "measure and tune the existing BatchedLabeller against shot 22086", which changes the effort and the done-when of the plan's two largest sections.
findings.text: the plan proposes §1 (§1 "the whole slice solve inside one compiled program with a fixed trip budget and masked convergence instead of the host ladder") and §2 (a batch of slices read in one fixed-shape program) as new machinery, but _make_solver already builds a dynamic-argument copy of the production trip loop with masked convergence and jax.vmap(one) at batched_labeller.py:725 already runs a fixed-shape batch and returns labelled_flux per element

findings.reason: the plan should name this kernel and state what the slower vmap probe measured, rather than leave the reader to discover the existing batched read.
findings.text: the plan's §2 proposes to "re-cast the pass so a batch of slices reads in one fixed-shape program", but this file already declares itself "the GPU inner-loop kernel for the batched corpus labeller (a jax.vmap over slices sharing one campaign grid)"

findings.reason: §5 is an extension of this method, so the plan should cite the owner it edits instead of describing the change as new behaviour.
findings.text: §5 proposes to "read the first iterate twice, the second read shadowed by the first", but the cold-start shadow it wants to give is the wall mask this method already returns ("the prior iterate's wall mask, or no mask on a cold start")

findings.reason: if _compiled_program already carries the trip, §1 is a tuning change to it rather than a new program, which removes a node from the plan.
findings.text: §1 wraps the whole-slice solve in a new compiled program, but _compiled_program already builds the compiled trip kernel and batched_labeller._make_solver already drives it; the plan adds a thin layer over both without saying why either cannot be extended

findings.reason: the plan should name one module that serves both single and batched slices, or it will maintain two compile paths that drift.
findings.text: §1 (one call is one slice) and §2 (a batch in one program) would add two entry points over the same _make_solver/_compiled_program machinery that BatchedLabeller already hides behind a single solve(), so the surface grows without a stated module boundary

findings.reason: §3's done-when (elongation and upper-point commands achieving within 5 percent) is a measurement of solve_shape_inverse(..., forward_solve=...) with the existing turning_point_relative_tolerance, so the section should extend or retune that owner rather than build a parallel outer loop.
findings.text: §3 proposes exactly what solve_shape_inverse already implements: "a bounded outer Newton loop refreshes the local current-to-turning-point tangent at that state, corrects the physical shape residual, and sends every correction through the same axis-admission line search" (module docstring line 29; the 20 kA ceiling and halving line search at lines 81 and 1224; the tolerance-bounded corrected loop at lines 1248-1255)

findings.reason: §6 reduces to pointing the existing sharded job at the decoder shot list and adding the digest-manifest field if it is absent, which is far smaller than the plan implies and must name these three owners.
findings.text: §6 asks for "one sharded job writing every shot's session as it lands with the per-slice conditioning flag and target source and a digest manifest, resumable by shot, with a completion receipt counting shots, slices, converged and qualified fractions and GPU-hours", which is already what scripts/labeller_batch/shard.py (writes steering sessions for one shard of MAST shots), scripts/labeller_batch/receipt.py (aggregates shot manifests into a completion receipt with the qualified fraction), and scripts/labeller_parallel/scheduler.py do

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §1 and §2 ask for a per-slice compiled program and a separate batched read over the same solver that BatchedLabeller already hides behind one solve(), so the design names no seam and would carry two parallel compile paths.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 duplicates the outer Newton loop that shape_inverse.solve_shape_inverse already owns under the same 20 kA ceiling and admission line search.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites no existing mechanism at all, while every section it proposes already has an owner in the tree (batched_labeller, shape_inverse, flux_surface_connectivity, the labeller_batch shard/receipt stack, forward_operator's cold-start wall mask).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §1's "whole slice solve inside one compiled program" layers over reduced_newton._compiled_program and batched_labeller._make_solver without saying why those cannot be extended.
